parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Aqueous solutions of copper(II) salts contain $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ ions.

Equilibrium 3 and equilibrium 4 show two reactions of these ions.

equilibrium 3 $\quad [\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \text{Cu}(\text{OH})_2(\text{s}) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$

equilibrium 4 $\quad [\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 4\text{NH}_3(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons [\text{Cu}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain why a precipitate is formed when $\text{NaOH}(\text{aq})$ is added dropwise to $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}(\text{aq})$.
